raw_response:
I’m still planting cotton on all 13.1 mu this year. I’ve done this for many years, and on my land cotton is steady if I manage the water and fertilizer on time. Wheat-maize can bring cash too, but for my family’s situation the cotton schedule fits better, and I know this crop well. The extension guy says not to push fertilizer too hard all at once, so I’ll split it. I usually watch the stand first, then decide whether to add a bit more at squaring. With well water available, I won’t let the field stay too dry at seedling stage and flowering stage, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate too many times unless the rain is really short. Family labor is limited because some people work outside, so I’ll keep the plan simple: machine or animal-drawn tillage if I can hire it cheaply, family members for most field watching and picking, and a little hired help if picking comes together too fast.
